newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Koh Brothers to list another subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Koh Brothers to list another subsidiary.

text.p: Construction company Koh Brothers Group Ltd plans to list another one of its subsidiaries shortly, managing director Tiak Chye Koh told a news conference on Thursday.
"The subsidiaries will be listed when the time comes. We hope it would be quite soon to list one of them," Koh said.
He said the subsidiary would be from a core contributor to the company.
Aside from construction, already effectively represented through the parent company, the group's core divisions are building materials and real estate.
Koh said the listing of the subsidiary would depend on the company's results and requirements of the stock exchange as well as market timing.
The group is targetting a more equitable contribution from its three core divisions, with each contributing a third in the future.
Construction now contributes about 35 percent to earnings, building materials and real estate combined about 40 percent and equipment sales and leisure and hospitality 20-25 percent.

Koh said while construction was a significant contributor, building materials and equipment sales and rental activities and property development in Singapore have gained importance over the last couple of years.
Koh said the company has about S$700 million worth of construction contracts in hand and was confident of securing more public sector projects.
"We will also be targetting more at value-added design-and-build construction projects," Koh said.

He said construction has been diversified overseas in places like China, where the company has undertaken a reclamation project, and India, where it has won a tender to design and build a flyover in Hyderabad.

The group hopes overseas contributions would grow to 10-15 percent over the next two-three years from below 10 percent now. On Thursday, the company announced it had clinched two construction contracts in Singapore, worth S$203.69 million.

Subsidiary Koh Brothers Building & Civil Engineering Contractor (Pte) Ltd (KBCE) won a S$161 million contract from the Port of Singapore Authority (PSA) to build a container stacking yard and a S$42.69 million project to design and build the Singapore Cancer Centre.
According to executive director Tan Hwa Peng, the two projects would only start contributing to the group's earnings in 1998, when both projects are scheduled for completion.

Koh said the strategy of investing in freehold properties in prime districts has left the company unscathed despite a current slowdown in residential property. It plans to launch The Capri at Stevens Road and The Sierra in Holland Road over the next few months.

The company has also undertaken a S$210 million joint development of a commercial and residential complex next to the Sembawang Mass Rapid Transit station. Feasibilty studies would be taken to expand overseas into China, Malaysia and Indonesia.
In leisure and hospitality, Koh said the company would continue to focus on budget hotels. A second hotel, the 134-room Stamford Inn, would be opened shortly.
In September, the group reported a 31 percent increase in interim turnover to S$118.4 million and a net profit of S$2.27 million.
